{"passages":[{"reference":"19.6","text":"And Simon said, “When I have discussed with you each of the points I proposed and shown you the cause of evil, then I will also answer what you have said and demonstrate that the God whom you call blameless is liable to blame.”

And Peter said, “Since, from what you have been saying from the beginning, I perceive that you are intent on nothing other than subjecting God to blame as the leader of evil, I have resolved to accompany you along every path you wish and show that God is beyond all blame.”

And Simon said, “You say these things as one who loves the one you have taken to be God, but you are not speaking the truth.”

And Peter said, “But you, as an evil man who hates the God you have failed to know, let loose blasphemous words.”

And Simon said, “Remember that you compared me to a leader of evil.”

And Peter said, “I confess that I lied when I compared you to the evil one, for I was compelled to do so because I could not find anyone equal to you or even worse. That is why I compared you to the evil one, for you prove to be much more wicked than even the leader of evil. No one can show that the evil one has spoken against God, but all of us who are present can attest that you boldly denounce him.”

And Simon said, “One who seeks the truth owes it to no one to concede anything contrary to what is. Otherwise, why does he seek at all? What then? Can I not also, setting aside an exact investigation of the facts, spend all my time praising a God whom I do not know?”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"θεὸν ὃν νενόμικας","chosen":"the one you have taken to be God","rationale":"The perfect of νομίζω presents Peter as having regarded or supposed this one to be God; “the God in whom you have believed” is possible but less directly reflects the verb’s evaluative sense."},{"source_quote":"ὡς κακίας ἡγεμόνα τὸν θεὸν ὑποβάλλειν μέμψει","chosen":"subjecting God to blame as the leader of evil","rationale":"ὑποβάλλειν μέμψει depicts placing or exposing someone under censure, while ὡς κακίας ἡγεμόνα gives the alleged basis of the blame."},{"source_quote":"τὸν πονηρὸν οὐδεὶς κατειπόντα θεοῦ δεῖξαι δύναται","chosen":"No one can show that the evil one has spoken against God","rationale":"καταλέγω here means speak against, denounce, or malign; the rendering does not import the stronger claim that he never otherwise opposes God."},{"source_quote":"οὐδὲν οὐδενὶ ὀφείλει παρὰ τὸ ὂν χαρίζεσθαι","chosen":"owes it to no one to concede anything contrary to what is","rationale":"χαρίζεσθαι can mean grant a favor or make a concession, and παρὰ τὸ ὄν contrasts such favor with reality as it is."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ἐγὼ οὐ δύναμαι, παρεὶς ἀκριβοῦν τὰ πράγματα, εἰς ἐγκώμιον οὗ μὴ ἐπίσταμαι θεοῦ τὸν πάντα μου δαπανᾶν χρόνον;","chosen":"Can I not also, setting aside an exact investigation of the facts, spend all my time praising a God whom I do not know?","rationale":"The printed question treats οὐ δύναμαι interrogatively. οὗ μὴ ἐπίσταμαι θεοῦ is rendered as an attracted relative construction referring to the unknown God."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"19.7","text":"And Peter said, “You are not blessed enough to praise him, nor indeed are you able to do this good thing, for then you would be full of him. For this is what our teacher, who does not lie, said: ‘A mouth speaks from the heart’s abundance.’ Therefore you, overflowing with an evil purpose caused by ignorance, speak against the only good God, and you do not yet suffer in proportion to what you dared to say. If you suppose there will be no judgment, perhaps you actually think there is no God. Therefore, because you fail to recognize such great patience on his part, you drive him still further toward desperate action.”

And Simon said, “Do not hope to cow me with fear so that I refrain from asking you what is true in the examples. I long so greatly for truth that, for its sake, I would not hesitate even to take on danger. But concerning the points I proposed to you at the beginning—if indeed you have anything to say—speak now.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Οὔτε τοσοῦτον εἶ μακάριος αὐτὸν ὑμνεῖν","chosen":"You are not blessed enough to praise him","rationale":"τοσοῦτον with the infinitive expresses the degree required for praising God, not merely the quantity of praise."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ περισσεύματος καρδίας στόμα λαλεῖ","chosen":"A mouth speaks from the heart’s abundance","rationale":"The rendering follows the wording supplied here rather than harmonizing it with a familiar canonical form; the Greek has neither “the mouth” nor an added possessive."},{"source_quote":"περισσευόμενος προαιρέσει κακῇ ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ","chosen":"overflowing with an evil purpose caused by ignorance","rationale":"προαίρεσις denotes a chosen disposition, purpose, or moral intention. The causal dative ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ associates that purpose with ignorance."},{"source_quote":"τῆς τοσαύτης αὐτοῦ μακροθυμίας οὐκ ἀντιλαμβανόμενος ἐπὶ πλεῖον πρὸς ἀπόνοιαν αὐτὸν ἐκτείνεις","chosen":"because you fail to recognize such great patience on his part, you drive him still further toward desperate action","rationale":"The masculine αὐτόν most directly refers to God, making him the object of ἐκτείνεις. ἀπόνοια can denote desperation, recklessness, or drastic resolve. An alternative contextual interpretation is “you go still further into recklessness,” but that would require taking αὐτόν loosely or supplying a different object."},{"source_quote":"φόβῳ δυσωπήσειν με μὴ ζητεῖν σοι τῶν παραδειγμάτων τὰ ἀληθῆ","chosen":"cow me with fear so that I refrain from asking you what is true in the examples","rationale":"δυσωπέω can mean shame, overawe, or intimidate. The infinitive with μή states the result Simon rejects, while σοι marks Peter as the person from whom an answer is sought."},{"source_quote":"εἴγε εἰπεῖν ἔχεις","chosen":"if indeed you have anything to say","rationale":"The idiom literally concerns having something available to say, not merely possessing the physical ability to speak."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"19.8","text":"And Peter said, “Since you force us to dare to speak after having exactly traced out God’s methods—and this though we are humans unable to ascertain precisely even the methods of those like ourselves—then, at least for the sake of those standing by, I will discuss what you wish instead of maintaining the most reverent silence. I agree with you that there is a certain leader of evil, about whose origin Scripture did not dare to say either something true or something false. Nevertheless, let us explore together, from many angles, how he came to be—if indeed he came to be—and let us choose from among the apparent possibilities the one that speaks more reverently. For this is securely inferred from what is probable: namely, that one should accord God the more reverent account, especially in this way, when all suspicions have been cleared away and another adequate and safer supposition is available. Nevertheless, even before the investigation I promise you that every path of inquiry can show him alone—God—to be beyond blame.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὰς τοῦ θεοῦ τέχνας ἀκριβῶς ἐφευρόντας λέγειν","chosen":"to speak after having exactly traced out God’s methods","rationale":"τέχναι can denote arts, devices, designs, or methods. “Methods” fits the inquiry into how God might have acted without reducing the phrase to physical craftsmanship."},{"source_quote":"οὗ τὴν γένεσιν ἡ γραφὴ οὔτε ἀληθὲς οὔτε ψευδὲς εἰπεῖν ἐτόλμησεν","chosen":"about whose origin Scripture did not dare to say either something true or something false","rationale":"The paired negatives portray Scripture as making no pronouncement about the origin. The wording is preserved rather than simplified to “Scripture says nothing.”"},{"source_quote":"τῶν δοκούντων τὸ εὐφημότερον ἑλώμεθα","chosen":"let us choose from among the apparent possibilities the one that speaks more reverently","rationale":"τὰ δοκοῦντα may mean apparent possibilities or proposed opinions. εὐφημότερον is comparative and favors the account that speaks more auspiciously or reverently of God."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ τῶν εἰκότων λαμβάνεται τοῦτο βεβαίως","chosen":"this is securely inferred from what is probable","rationale":"εἰκότα are probable considerations rather than certainties. The apparently tense combination of probability and secure inference is retained."},{"source_quote":"ἄμεμπτον αὐτὸν μόνον δύναται δεῖξαι τὸν θεόν","chosen":"can show him alone—God—to be beyond blame","rationale":"μόνον is taken with αὐτόν, identifying God alone as blameless. It could instead be attached adverbially to δύναται, yielding “can only show God to be blameless.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ ἐκ τῶν εἰκότων λαμβάνεται τοῦτο βεβαίως, ὃ μὲν ὅτι θεῷ τὸ εὐφημότερον δοῦναι πρέπει, ταύτῃ μᾶλλον πασῶν ὑπονοιῶν καθαρθεισῶν καὶ ἄλλης ἱκανῆς καὶ ἀκινδυνοτέρας παρακειμένης ὑποψίας","issue":"The supplied, image-checked wording is syntactically compressed, especially at ὃ μὲν ὅτι, and no balancing δέ follows μὲν. The translation takes the clause as introducing the principle that the more reverent account should be accorded to God. An alternative is to understand ὃ μὲν as beginning an unfinished first reason. No alteration to the selected reading is assumed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"19.9","text":"Nevertheless, as you said, if the evil one is something that came into being, then either he came to be as a living creature, or was substantially put forth by God, or was compounded externally; or his choice resulted from the compounding, or his choice happened to arise without compounding and without God’s counsel. Or he came to be from things that did not exist, or by God from what exists nowhere in any way; or else outside God there was either lifeless or animate matter from which he came to be; or he created himself; or he came into being by God; or he is one of the things that exist in relation to something else; or he always existed. For we cannot say that he does not exist, since we agreed together that he exists.

And Simon said, “You have divided all the paths concerning him well—the main question about him. It is now my part, after scrutinizing the division, to show you that the Creator is liable to blame; but your task is to prove, as you promised, that he is beyond all blame. I wonder whether you will be able to do so. First, if the evil one came into being from God as a living creature, he consequently possesses the same evil as the one who put him forth.”

And Peter said, “Not necessarily. For we see many among human beings who are good yet have fathered bad children, others who are bad yet have had good children, still others who are bad yet produce good offspring, and others who are good yet have become parents of both bad and good children. Thus the first man who was created fathered the unrighteous Cain and the righteous Abel.”

In response Simon said, “You act foolishly by discussing God while using human examples.”

And Peter said, “Then tell us about God without using human examples, while still making it possible for what you say to be understood. But you will not be able to do so.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰ γενητός ἐστιν","chosen":"if the evil one is something that came into being","rationale":"γενητός can mean generated, originated, or created. The broader wording avoids deciding in advance which mode of origination the subsequent alternatives will support."},{"source_quote":"οὐσιωδῶς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ προβέβληται","chosen":"was substantially put forth by God","rationale":"προβάλλω can describe putting forth or emanation, and οὐσιωδῶς indicates that this occurs with respect to substance. The antecedent of αὐτοῦ is understood contextually as God."},{"source_quote":"ἔξω κέκραται","chosen":"was compounded externally","rationale":"κεράννυμι denotes mixing or compounding. ἔξω may mean outside God or externally; the Greek does not explicitly state the reference point here."},{"source_quote":"ἢ ἐκτὸς ἦν θεοῦ ἢ ὕλη ἄψυχος οὖσα ἢ ἔμψυχος ὅθεν γέγονεν","chosen":"or else outside God there was either lifeless or animate matter from which he came to be","rationale":"The rendering takes ἐκτὸς θεοῦ with the existence of matter and treats ἄψυχος and ἔμψυχος as its alternatives. It is also possible to divide the sequence as “or he was outside God; or there was lifeless or animate matter from which he came to be.”"},{"source_quote":"ἢ τῶν πρὸς τὶ ἐστὶν","chosen":"or he is one of the things that exist in relation to something else","rationale":"τὰ πρός τι is philosophical language for relative or relational entities—things defined through a relation to something else."},{"source_quote":"Καλῶς πάσας αὐτοῦ τὰς ὁδοὺς διεῖλες, τὸ κεφάλαιον αὐτοῦ","chosen":"You have divided all the paths concerning him well—the main question about him","rationale":"τὸ κεφάλαιον may denote a heading, summary, chief point, or principal question. The punctuation leaves its precise attachment compressed, so the translation treats it as an appositional summary of the division."},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτῆς τοῦ προβάλλοντος κακίας τυγχάνει","chosen":"he consequently possesses the same evil as the one who put him forth","rationale":"The subject remains the evil one, while τοῦ προβάλλοντος identifies the producer whose evil Simon infers from the offspring’s nature."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"19.10","text":"For instance, what did you say at the outset? “If the evil one came into being from God, being of the same substance as God, then God too is evil.” But when I showed from the very example you yourself supplied that bad people come from good people and good people from bad people, you did not accept it, saying that the example was human. Therefore I in turn do not now accept that God has been begotten, because begetting belongs to human beings, not to God. But neither can God be good or evil, just or unjust, nor indeed prudent, a living creature, or anything else that can belong to human beings, for such qualities belong to human beings. And if, when investigating God, we must not ascribe to him the good qualities belonging to human beings, there is nothing left to conceive, say, or investigate except this alone: the matter of his purpose, which he himself permitted us to understand, so that, when judged, we may be without excuse concerning what we knew but did not keep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰ ἐκ θεοῦ ὁ πονηρὸς γεγένηται, τῆς αὐτῆς αὐτῷ ὢν οὐσίας, καὶ πονηρός ἐστιν","chosen":"If the evil one came into being from God, being of the same substance as God, then God too is evil","rationale":"The subject of the final ἐστιν is implicit. Taking it as God avoids the tautology that the evil one is evil and matches Peter’s summary of Simon’s attempt to blame the Creator. A formally possible but contextually weak rendering is “then he too is evil.”"},{"source_quote":"ἐξ οὗπερ αὐτὸς ἔδωκας παραδείγματος","chosen":"from the very example you yourself supplied","rationale":"The emphatic οὗπερ and αὐτός attribute the example to Simon, even though Peter developed its comparison in the preceding exchange."},{"source_quote":"οὐδὲ τὸ γεγεννῆσθαι θεὸν παραδέχομαι","chosen":"I do not now accept that God has been begotten","rationale":"The perfect passive infinitive presents God as having undergone generation. The surprising assertion is retained as part of Peter’s reductio rather than changed into “God begets.”"},{"source_quote":"οὔτε μὴν φρόνιμος ἢ ζῷον","chosen":"nor indeed prudent, a living creature","rationale":"φρόνιμος means prudent, sensible, or practically wise. ζῷον is rendered broadly as “a living creature,” preserving Peter’s analogy with human predicates."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τῆς προαιρέσεως αὐτοῦ","chosen":"the matter of his purpose","rationale":"προαίρεσις can mean choice, intention, purpose, or moral disposition. Here it refers to the divine purpose made knowable for human accountability."},{"source_quote":"ὅπως κρινόμενοι ἀναπολόγητοι ὦμεν περὶ ὧν γνόντες οὐκ ἐφυλάξαμεν","chosen":"so that, when judged, we may be without excuse concerning what we knew but did not keep","rationale":"ἀναπολόγητοι means without a defense or excuse, and φυλάσσω here concerns observing or keeping what was known."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀνθρώ- .πινον","issue":"The supplied reading interrupts the single word with a hyphen, whitespace, and a period. The context and the surviving letters clearly indicate the adjective ἀνθρώπινον, “human.” This is treated as an apparent typographical interruption, not as missing wording or a lacuna.","proposed_reading":"ἀνθρώπινον","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
